subject: Kernel Labs SDK integration: tracer + prompt telemetry sprint plan

From: Eva Martin <eva@kernellabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kernel Labs + Redwood — lightweight tracer & prompt telemetry pilot

Hi Vanessa,

Hope you’re well — I’m Eva on Partnerships at Kernel Labs. We build a lightweight SDK for prompt & model-invocation telemetry (traces + token-aligned spans) that many ISVs (LangChain, LlamaIndex integrators) have started shipping as a plugin.

We’ve been validating a runtime adapter that forwards compact spans and prompt context to a tracing intake (or an S3 sink) and have a small compatibility shim for LangChain callbacks and LlamaIndex retrievers. We think Redwood’s serving runtime is a great place to run a first pilot — reduced per-token telemetry cost and explicit mapping between KV cache events and model spans would help both our customers and Redwood customers.

Quick summary attached (kernel-sdk-proposal.pdf). High-level asks:
- A short pilot (3 sprints) to ship a runtime adapter + LangChain callback sample app.
- Access to a dedicated sandbox endpoint or a dev cluster for validation.
- A technical sync to align on auth, SLOs, and data retention.

Proposed times for a 30–45m call: Wed May 24 10:00–11:00 PDT, Thurs May 25 09:00–11:00 PDT. We’re flexible.

Thanks — happy to share a quick demo beforehand.

Best,
Eva Martin
Partnerships, Kernel Labs
https://kernellabs.com

Attachment: kernel-sdk-proposal.pdf

Hi Eva — thanks for the note and the proposal. I’m the Partner Lead for ISV integrations; looping in Kimberly (product infra) and Marissa (isv partnerships) so they can scope technical acceptance and go/no-go criteria.

High level we’re interested — two quick asks before we lock a 3-sprint plan:
1) Can you confirm exactly what parts of the trace payload include prompt text (we have customers with strict PII policies)?
2) Do you have an auth model for the adapter (signed API keys, mTLS, or token-forwarding)?

Next steps I propose (we can finalize on the call):
- Phase 0: NDA + legal + brief security questionnaire (we can share SOC2 evidence if needed).
- Phase 1 (sprint 1): Instrumentation shim (LangChain callback + basic LlamaIndex retriever hooks) and a sample app that demonstrates token-aligned spans.
- Phase 2 (sprint 2): Runtime adapter for Redwood that can receive compact spans and either forward to a tracing backend or write to a secure bucket (customer-controlled).
- Phase 3 (sprint 3): Canary pilot with one internal Redwood app and a customer-facing sample.

I attached our internal integration acceptance checklist to speed reviews (redwood-integration-acceptance-checklist.xlsx).

Wed/Thu times look good — Kimberly, Marissa, any preferences? Eva, let us know which slot you prefer and we’ll book a calendar invite.

—

Thanks Vanessa — quick technical notes from infra/product.

On data model: we need a clear opt-in for prompt text. For the pilot please provide a field-level schema where prompt_text can be redacted or hashed before it leaves the runtime. Kernel saying you can emit token-aligned spans is great — we’ll need an example payload (json schema) showing token indices and span boundaries.

On auth: our preference for partner adapters is signed short-lived tokens (JWT with partner id) + optional mutual TLS for high-trust customers. We can support static API keys for a sandbox but not for production.

Operational concerns:
- Tracing cardinality: please keep per-request event counts bounded. Large prompting loops easily explode telemetry volume.
- KV-cache correlation: we need correlation IDs surfaced in spans so we can link cache hits/misses with model tokens.
- Retention: default retention for pilot artifacts should be 30 days unless the customer opts in for longer.

Compatibility notes: LangChain callback integration should expose two hooks: on_prompt (pre-invocation) and on_response (post-invocation) — those are enough to do token-aligned spans in most customers. For LlamaIndex retrievers, prefer emitting a retriever_span with doc_id and retrieval_score.

If Kernel can provide a minimal Node and Python sample (no more than ~80 lines) that plugs into LangChain’s callback interface, we can spin up a sandbox test by Thurs.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Principal Product Manager, Runtime Integrations
redwood.com

Hi Kim / Vanessa — thanks, great notes. Quick answers inline: 

- Prompt text: we support three modes: cleartext, redaction (replace with [REDACTED]), and token-hash (deterministic token hashing). For the pilot we recommend token-hash by default; we can enable cleartext only with a signed customer opt-in.

- Example payload: attached folder in Drive has a sample payload and two minimal adapters (python/node). We’ll also drop a small sample that integrates with LangChain’s on_prompt/on_response hooks. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Kern3lProposal

- Auth: sandbox: static API key. Prod recommended: short-lived JWT + optional mTLS for enterprise.

- Cardinality: our adapter supports sampling rules (1-in-N spans) and prefix aggregation to keep event counts bounded. We’ll expose config flags for the runtime adapter to control sampling and prefix window sizes.

- Retention: default 30 days, configurable per-customer and per-bucket. We are happy to ship a retention policy manifest that you can review.

We can get a Python LangChain sample to you by EOD Wed (24th). For the call, Thurs May 25 09:30–10:00 PDT works for our engineering lead — is that OK?

Thanks —
Eva Martin
Partnerships, Kernel Labs
